sections.heading: Loop Structures and Iterative Solutions
sections.body: This week's focus is on the implementation of iterative solutions using loop structures. The topics covered are 'for', 'while', 'do-while', and 'break/continue'. These constructs allow for repeated execution of code until a specific condition is met, making them essential in solving problems that require multiple iterations.

sections.heading: Hands-on Laboratory Exercises
sections.body: In this week's activities, students will engage in hands-on laboratory exercises to practice and reinforce their understanding of loop structures. These practical sessions will help develop problem-solving skills and prepare for the upcoming assessment.

sections.heading: Assessment Preparation
sections.body: The planned assessment is a practical exercise that tests students' ability to implement loop structures in programming. The questions are designed to evaluate their understanding of 'for', 'while', and 'do-while' loops, as well as the use of 'break/continue'.

sections.heading: Assessment Questions
sections.body:
1. What is the purpose of a loop structure in programming? (A) To repeat a set of instructions until a condition is met.
(B) To execute code continuously without any conditions.
(C) To break out of an infinite loop prematurely.
(D) To skip over certain lines of code based on conditions.

2. Which loop structure should be used when the number of iterations is unknown? (A) 'for' loop.
(B) 'while' loop.
(C) 'do-while' loop.
(D) None of these.

3. What does the 'continue' statement do in a loop? (A) It skips over the rest of the current iteration and moves to the next one.
(B) It terminates the entire loop execution.
(C) It repeats the current iteration until the condition is met.
(D) It changes the value of the loop variable.
